title: Drop Dialysis Protocol
author: Ken Christensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc53iy8n
materials: Float a 13mm or 25 mm diameter, Type-VS Millipore membrane (MF type, VS filter, mean pore size = 0.025 μm, Millipore, Inc. #VSWP02500 or #VSWP01300) shiny side up on the dialysis buffer. Allow the floating filter to wet completely (~5 minutes) before proceeding. Make sure there are no air bubbles trapped under the filter.

steps.title: Prepare dialysis buffer
steps.instruction: Pour 30–100 mL of dialysis buffer (either double‑distilled water or 1X TE: 10 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) into a Petri dish or beaker.

steps.title: Apply DNA droplet to filter
steps.instruction: Place a few µL of the DNA sample onto the dialysis filter; multiple samples can be processed on one filter if size permits.

substeps.instruction: If the sample contains excess phenol or chloroform, the droplet will not stay centered—stop the dialysis and remove organics, typically by alcohol precipitation, before proceeding.
If the droplet remains centered, optionally add any remaining sample volume onto the same membrane.
Dialysis against double‑distilled water is recommended when downstream steps are sensitive to EDTA.
Practice pipetting onto buffer droplets beforehand if hand stability is an issue.

steps.title: Incubate dialysis
steps.instruction: Cover the Petri dish or beaker and allow dialysis to proceed for 15 minutes to 4 hours, ensuring the sample does not flip or become submerged in buffer.

steps.title: Recover DNA from membrane
steps.instruction: Collect the DNA droplet with a micro‑pipette into a microcentrifuge tube and rinse the membrane spot with 50 µL of water or 1X TE (10 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0), adding the rinse to the same tube.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the droplet using a micro‑pipette and transfer to a microcentrifuge tube.
Rinse the membrane spot with 50 µL of water or 1X TE and add the rinse to the tube.

steps.title: Quantify recovered DNA
steps.instruction: Determine DNA concentration by agarose‑gel electrophoresis or spectrophotometry.
